# Mara Ellis — fictional author brief

This is authored fiction, not private notes or a reconstructed real person's
history. Mara works on public participation at a small museum, volunteers at a
community workshop, helps her mother with transport and appointments, gardens,
cycles and attends a pottery class. The place, people, quotations and events
are invented. The source period is January 2024 through December 2025, with a
small pre-existing notebook and a backdated fictional clipping import.

Mara knows when her exhibition ends, when the repair cafe begins and why the
induction vocabulary changes. Reminding her of these facts is usually redundant.
She has not initially joined up all the dependencies on one person across work,
care and volunteering. Her Maintenance and Listening notes develop through real
text revisions. The useful question should point to concrete passages and leave
her room to reject a proposed connection.

She values fewer unwanted obligations, practical choice, safe refusals and
clear handovers. A suggestion that creates work merely because a note is short,
a project is finished or an object is imperfect may miss her intentions. An
unexpected metaphor or playful transformation can still be useful without
detecting a statistical event.

The evaluation ledger is external to the ingested vault. It was written before
the first evaluation, not inferred from successful outputs. The corpus is an
initial usefulness proxy; its author cannot supply independent real-user ratings.
